newsitem.title: USA: Rain storms should slow Midwest corn planting.
newsitem.headline: Rain storms should slow Midwest corn planting.

text.p: Two storm systems due to spread through the Midwest beginning late Tuesday should halt spring planting in much of Iowa, northern Illinois and northern Indiana for most of the week, forecasters said.

"There are two (rain) systems with Iowa's name on them," said Joel Burgio, Weather Services Corp meteorologist, who expects 0.5 to 2.0 inches in much of eastern Nebraska, Iowa and northern Illinois from each system.
Missouri, southern Illinois and southern Indiana may receive 0.25 to 1.0 inch through Wednesday.
The second rain event was due in the western Midwest Friday and spreading east Saturday and Sunday, with similar amounts as the first, said Burgio.
"They could be shut down for a while," Burgio said of farmers' planting efforts.
Fred Gesser, Weather Express Inc meteorologist, expects 60 to 70 percent coverage across the northern half of Iowa, northern Illinois and northern Indiana.
High temperatures in the 70s degrees Fahrenheit Tuesday in Iowa and Illinois will be replaced Wednesday by below normal temperatures with highs in the 50s into next week, he said.
The rain may subside next week but below-normal temperatures should remain, said Gesser.
"There is a noticable lack of major weather systems for next week," he said of conditions expected in the Midwest.
